   202	    (hI : SpectralHomogeneous μ alpha) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ]
   203	    (ha0 : 0 < alpha) (ha2 : alpha < 2) (q : ℝ) (hq : 0 < q) :

   140	/-! ### Lower bounds of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` -/
   141	
   142	/-- The first lower bound of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (main TeX line
   143	838, proof line 913), for any measure (in particular `mμ`): `0 ≤ N_{1,S}(θ)`
   144	for every set `S` and `a > 0`, since the integrand `λ^{a-1} R(θ+λ)` is
   145	nonnegative on `(0,∞)`. -/
   146	theorem N1on_nonneg (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (ha : 0 < a) :
   147	    0 ≤ N1on a θ S μ := by
   148	  have := Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos ha
   149	  unfold N1on
   150	  refine mul_nonneg (by positivity) (integral_nonneg_of_ae ?_)
   151	  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae ae_L0_pos] with l hl
   152	  exact mul_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg hl.le _) (resolvent_nonneg _ _)
   153	
   154	/-- The second lower bound of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (main TeX line
   155	839, proof lines 900-911), for any s-finite measure (in particular `mμ`) with
   156	`∫(1+|ξ|²)⁻¹ dμ < ∞` and `μ{0} = 0`, `0 < a < 1`, `θ > 0`, `S` measurable:
   157	`0 ≤ N_{2,S}(θ)²`, since `N_{2,S}(θ)² = ∫_{S ∩ (0,∞)} w_θ` (`N2onSq_eq`) and
   158	`w_θ ≥ 0`. -/
   159	theorem N2onSq_nonneg (μ : Measure (Rd d)) [SFinite μ]
   160	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ) (hμ0 : μ {0} = 0)
   161	    (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hθ : 0 < θ) (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
   162	    0 ≤ N2onSq a θ S μ := by
   163	  rw [(N2onSq_eq μ hR hμ0 a θ S ha0 ha1 hθ hS).2.2]
   164	  refine integral_nonneg_of_ae ?_
   165	  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae ae_L0_pos] with l hl
   166	  exact weight_nonneg μ hR a θ l ha0 hθ hl
   167	
   168	/-- `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (main TeX lines 836-841, proof 894-913)
   169	in full, both lower and upper bounds, for a general measure: `μ` s-finite with
   170	`∫(1+|ξ|²)⁻¹ dμ < ∞` and `μ{0} = 0`, `0 < a < 1`, `θ > 0`, the integrand of
   171	`N₁(θ)` for `μ` integrable on `(0,∞)`, `g` measurable with values in `[0,1]`,
   172	`S ⊆ S'` measurable.  Conclusions: the integrand of `N_{1,g,S}` is integrable,
   173	`0 ≤ N_{1,g,S}(θ) ≤ N_{1,1,S'}(θ)`; the outer integrands of `N_{2,g,S}` and
   174	`N_{2,1,S'}` are integrable and `0 ≤ N_{2,g,S}(θ)² ≤ N_{2,1,S'}(θ)²`. -/
   175	theorem damped_multiplier_comparison (μ : Measure (Rd d)) [SFinite μ]
   176	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ) (hμ0 : μ {0} = 0)
   177	    (a θ : ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hθ : 0 < θ)
   178	    (hN : Integrable (fun l : ℝ => l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent μ (θ + l)) L0)
   179	    (g : Rd d → ℝ≥0) (hg : Measurable g) (hg1 : ∀ ξ, g ξ ≤ 1) (S S' : Set ℝ)
   180	    (hS : MeasurableSet S) (hS' : MeasurableSet S') (hSS : S ⊆ S') :
   181	    Integrable (fun l : ℝ => l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent (smoothed μ g) (θ + l)) L0 ∧
   182	      0 ≤ N1on a θ S (smoothed μ g) ∧ N1on a θ S (smoothed μ g) ≤ N1on a θ S' μ ∧
   183	      Integrable (N2onOuter a θ S (smoothed μ g)) P2 ∧ Integrable (N2onOuter a θ S' μ) P2 ∧
   184	      0 ≤ N2onSq a θ S (smoothed μ g) ∧ N2onSq a θ S (smoothed μ g) ≤ N2onSq a θ S' μ := by
   185	  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := N1on_smoothed_mono μ hR a θ ha0 hθ hN g hg hg1 S S' hSS
   186	  obtain ⟨h3, h4, h5⟩ := N2onSq_smoothed_mono μ hR hμ0 a θ ha0 ha1 hθ g hg hg1 S S' hS hS' hSS
   187	  exact ⟨h1, N1on_nonneg a θ S _ ha0, h2, h3, h4,
   188	    N2onSq_nonneg _ (smoothed_hR μ g hg hg1 hR) (smoothed_zero μ g hμ0) a θ S ha0 ha1 hθ hS,
   189	    h5⟩

   191	/-! ### (i) The multiplier class and Gaussian multipliers -/
   192	
   193	/-- The multiplier class of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (TeX lines
   194	826-829): `g : ℝ^d → ℝ≥0` measurable with values in `[0,1]`. -/
   195	def IsMultiplier (g : Rd d → ℝ≥0) : Prop := Measurable g ∧ ∀ ξ, g ξ ≤ 1
   196	
   197	/-- The class is closed under pointwise products (TeX lines 845-846 and
   198	915-916: "products of multipliers in `[0,1]` depending only on `ξ`"). -/
   199	theorem IsMultiplier.mul {g h : Rd d → ℝ≥0} (hg : IsMultiplier g) (hh : IsMultiplier h) :
   200	    IsMultiplier (g * h) :=
   201	  ⟨hg.1.mul hh.1, fun ξ => by
   202	    simpa using mul_le_one' (hg.2 ξ) (hh.2 ξ)⟩
   203	
   204	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route (no manuscript step).  Multiplying the
   205	spectral measure by `g` and then by `h` (both measurable) is multiplying it by
   206	`g h`: `h(gμ) = (gh)μ`. -/
   207	theorem smoothed_smoothed (μ : Measure (Rd d)) {g h : Rd d → ℝ≥0} (hg : Measurable g)
   208	    (hh : Measurable h) : smoothed (smoothed μ g) h = smoothed μ (g * h) := by
   209	  unfold smoothed
   210	  rw [← withDensity_mul μ hg.coe_nnreal_ennreal hh.coe_nnreal_ennreal]
   211	  congr 1
   212	
   213	/-- The Gaussian multiplier `ξ ↦ e^{-η|ξ|²}`, as a function with values in
   214	`ℝ≥0`. -/
   215	def gaussMult (η : ℝ) (ξ : Rd d) : ℝ≥0 := ⟨Real.exp (-(η * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)), (Real.exp_pos _).le⟩
   216	
   217	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  The real value of `gaussMult`. -/
   218	theorem coe_gaussMult (η : ℝ) (ξ : Rd d) :
   219	    (gaussMult η ξ : ℝ) = Real.exp (-(η * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) := rfl
   220	
   221	/-- For `η ≥ 0` the Gaussian multiplier `e^{-η|ξ|²}` is in the class: it is
   222	measurable with values in `[0,1]` (TeX lines 845-846, 915-916). -/
   223	theorem isMultiplier_gaussMult (η : ℝ) (hη : 0 ≤ η) : IsMultiplier (gaussMult (d := d) η) := by
   224	  refine ⟨Measurable.subtype_mk (by fun_prop), fun ξ => ?_⟩
   225	  show Real.exp _ ≤ 1
   226	  rw [Real.exp_le_one_iff]
   227	  have := sq_nonneg ‖ξ‖
   228	  nlinarith

   230	/-! ### (ii) Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel preserves the mass -/
   231	
   232	/-- The centered Gaussian law on `ℝ^d` with covariance `v I` (`v ≥ 0`), the
   233	image of Mathlib's standard Gaussian `stdGaussian` under `x ↦ √v x`.  It stands
   234	for the heat kernel `p_η` of the TeX (lines 1674, 4698): `p_η = N(0, cη I)` for
   235	the source's normalization constant `c > 0` is `gaussKernel (c η)`. -/
   236	def gaussKernel (v : ℝ) : Measure (Rd d) :=
   237	  (stdGaussian (Rd d)).map fun x => Real.sqrt v • x
   238	
   239	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  `gaussKernel v` is a probability
   240	measure. -/
   241	instance isProbabilityMeasure_gaussKernel (v : ℝ) :
   242	    IsProbabilityMeasure (gaussKernel (d := d) v) := by
   243	  unfold gaussKernel
   244	  infer_instance

   246	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  Convolution with a probability measure
   247	preserves total mass: `(ρ * ν)(ℝ^d) = ν(ℝ^d)` for `ν` s-finite. -/
   248	theorem conv_univ (ρ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ρ] (ν : Measure (Rd d))
   249	    [SFinite ν] : (ρ ∗ ν) univ = ν univ := by
   250	  rw [Measure.conv, Measure.map_apply measurable_add MeasurableSet.univ, preimage_univ,
   251	    ← univ_prod_univ, Measure.prod_prod, measure_univ, one_mul]
   252	
   253	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  Under `GreenMass G`, every `G_s` with
   254	`s > 0` is a finite measure. -/
   255	theorem isFiniteMeasure_of_greenMass {G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)} (hG : GreenMass G) (s : ℝ)
   256	    (hs : 0 < s) : IsFiniteMeasure (G s) :=
   257	  ⟨by rw [hG.mass s hs]; exact ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top⟩
   258	
   259	/-- `GreenMass` is preserved by convolution with a probability measure `ρ`:
   260	`(ρ * G_s)(ℝ^d) = G_s(ℝ^d) = s` for `s > 0` (for `ρ` the Gaussian `p_η`: TeX
   261	lines 846-847, 916-917). -/
   262	theorem greenMass_conv (ρ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ρ]
   263	    {G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)} (hG : GreenMass G) : GreenMass (fun s => ρ ∗ G s) := by
   264	  refine ⟨fun s hs => ?_⟩
   265	  have := isFiniteMeasure_of_greenMass hG s hs
   266	  rw [conv_univ, hG.mass s hs]
   267	
   268	/-- The separate mass assertion for `N₀` (TeX lines 846-847, proof 916-917):
   269	smoothing the Green family by a probability measure `ρ` leaves `N₀` unchanged,
   270	`N₀^{ρ*G}(θ) = N₀^{G}(θ) = θ^{-2}` for `θ > 0`, with the integrand of `N₀^{ρ*G}`
   271	integrable on `(0,∞)`; hypothesis `GreenMass G`. -/
   272	theorem N0_conv (ρ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ρ]
   273	    {G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)} (hG : GreenMass G) (θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) :
   274	    IntegrableOn (fun s => Real.exp (-(θ * s)) * ((ρ ∗ G s) univ).toReal) (Ioi 0) ∧
   275	      N0 (fun s => ρ ∗ G s) θ = N0 G θ ∧ N0 (fun s => ρ ∗ G s) θ = θ ^ (-(2 : ℝ)) := by
   276	  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := N0_eq _ (greenMass_conv ρ hG) θ hθ
   277	  exact ⟨h1, h2.trans (N0_eq G hG θ hθ).2.symm, h2⟩
   278	
   279	/-- The Gaussian-smoothed wave Green measures `p * G_s` (`p = gaussKernel v`,
   280	`v ≥ 0` not needed) have mass `s` for `s > 0`, `d ∈ {1,2,3}`, and
   281	`N₀(θ) = θ^{-2}`, the value for the unsmoothed `G_s` (`WaveGreen.N0_waveGreen`). -/
   282	theorem gauss_waveGreen_mass (d : ℕ) (hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) (v θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) :
   283	    GreenMass (fun s => gaussKernel v ∗ waveGreen d s) ∧
   284	      IntegrableOn (fun s => Real.exp (-(θ * s)) *
   285	        ((gaussKernel v ∗ waveGreen d s) univ).toReal) (Ioi 0) ∧
   286	      N0 (fun s => gaussKernel v ∗ waveGreen d s) θ = N0 (waveGreen d) θ ∧
   287	      N0 (fun s => gaussKernel v ∗ waveGreen d s) θ = θ ^ (-(2 : ℝ)) :=
   288	  ⟨greenMass_conv _ (waveGreen_greenMass d hd),
   289	    N0_conv (gaussKernel v) (waveGreen_greenMass d hd) θ hθ⟩

   291	/-! ### (iii) Green smoothing as a Fourier multiplier -/
   292	
   293	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  The characteristic function of
   294	`gaussKernel v` (`v ≥ 0`):
   295	`∫ e^{i⟨x,ξ⟩} p(dx) = e^{-v|ξ|²/2}`. -/
   296	theorem charFun_gaussKernel (v : ℝ) (hv : 0 ≤ v) (ξ : Rd d) :
   297	    charFun (gaussKernel v) ξ = Complex.exp (-(v * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) / 2) := by
   298	  unfold gaussKernel
   299	  rw [charFun_map_smul, charFun_stdGaussian, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs,
   300	    abs_of_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg v)]
   301	  congr 1
   302	  have h2 : (√v * ‖ξ‖) ^ 2 = v * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 := by rw [mul_pow, Real.sq_sqrt hv]
   303	  rw [← Complex.ofReal_pow, h2]
   304	  push_cast
   305	  ring
   306	
   307	/-- Gaussian smoothing of a finite measure `G` multiplies its characteristic
   308	function by `e^{-v|ξ|²/2}` (`v ≥ 0`): `\widehat{p*G}(ξ) = e^{-v|ξ|²/2} Ĝ(ξ)`. -/
   309	theorem charFun_gaussKernel_conv (v : ℝ) (hv : 0 ≤ v) (G : Measure (Rd d)) [IsFiniteMeasure G]
   310	    (ξ : Rd d) :
   311	    charFun (gaussKernel v ∗ G) ξ = Complex.exp (-(v * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) / 2) * charFun G ξ := by
   312	  rw [charFun_conv, charFun_gaussKernel v hv]
   313	
   314	/-- For finite `G`, `H` and `v ≥ 0`, the product of the transforms of the
   315	smoothed measures is the multiplier `e^{-v|ξ|²}` (`gaussMult v`) times the
   316	product of the transforms:
   317	`\widehat{p*G}(ξ) \overline{\widehat{p*H}(ξ)} = e^{-v|ξ|²} Ĝ(ξ) \overline{Ĥ(ξ)}`. -/
   318	theorem charFun_pair_gaussKernel_conv (v : ℝ) (hv : 0 ≤ v) (G H : Measure (Rd d))
   319	    [IsFiniteMeasure G] [IsFiniteMeasure H] (ξ : Rd d) :
   320	    charFun (gaussKernel v ∗ G) ξ * conj (charFun (gaussKernel v ∗ H) ξ) =
   321	      (gaussMult v ξ : ℝ) * (charFun G ξ * conj (charFun H ξ)) := by
   322	  rw [charFun_gaussKernel_conv v hv G, charFun_gaussKernel_conv v hv H, coe_gaussMult, map_mul,

   595	    (h : HomogCovariance 1 alpha alpha0 Γ μ) (v : ℝ) (hv : 0 ≤ v) (θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ)
   596	    (S S' : Set ℝ) (hS : MeasurableSet S) (hS' : MeasurableSet S') (hSS : S ⊆ S') :
   597	    Integrable (N2GreenOuter alpha0 θ S μ (waveGreen 1)) P2 ∧
   598	      N2GreenSq alpha0 θ S μ (waveGreen 1) = (N2onSq alpha0 θ S μ : ℂ) ∧
   599	      Integrable (N2GreenOuter alpha0 θ S μ (fun s => gaussKernel v ∗ waveGreen 1 s)) P2 ∧
   600	      N2GreenSq alpha0 θ S μ (fun s => gaussKernel v ∗ waveGreen 1 s) =
   601	        (N2onSq alpha0 θ S (smoothed μ (gaussMult v)) : ℂ) ∧
   602	      Integrable (N2onOuter alpha0 θ S (smoothed μ (gaussMult v))) P2 ∧
   603	      Integrable (N2onOuter alpha0 θ S' μ) P2 ∧
   604	      0 ≤ N2onSq alpha0 θ S (smoothed μ (gaussMult v)) ∧
   605	      N2onSq alpha0 θ S (smoothed μ (gaussMult v)) ≤ N2onSq alpha0 θ S' μ :=
   606	  damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_paper h greenFourier_one v hv θ hθ S S' hS hS' hSS

   140	/-! ### Lower bounds of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` -/
   141	
   142	/-- The first lower bound of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (main TeX line
   143	838, proof line 913), for any measure (in particular `mμ`): `0 ≤ N_{1,S}(θ)`
   144	for every set `S` and `a > 0`, since the integrand `λ^{a-1} R(θ+λ)` is
   145	nonnegative on `(0,∞)`. -/
   146	theorem N1on_nonneg (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (ha : 0 < a) :
   147	    0 ≤ N1on a θ S μ := by
   148	  have := Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos ha
   149	  unfold N1on
   150	  refine mul_nonneg (by positivity) (integral_nonneg_of_ae ?_)
   151	  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae ae_L0_pos] with l hl
   152	  exact mul_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg hl.le _) (resolvent_nonneg _ _)
   153	
   154	/-- The second lower bound of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (main TeX line
   155	839, proof lines 900-911), for any s-finite measure (in particular `mμ`) with
   156	`∫(1+|ξ|²)⁻¹ dμ < ∞` and `μ{0} = 0`, `0 < a < 1`, `θ > 0`, `S` measurable:
   157	`0 ≤ N_{2,S}(θ)²`, since `N_{2,S}(θ)² = ∫_{S ∩ (0,∞)} w_θ` (`N2onSq_eq`) and
   158	`w_θ ≥ 0`. -/
   159	theorem N2onSq_nonneg (μ : Measure (Rd d)) [SFinite μ]
   160	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ) (hμ0 : μ {0} = 0)
   161	    (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hθ : 0 < θ) (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
   162	    0 ≤ N2onSq a θ S μ := by
   163	  rw [(N2onSq_eq μ hR hμ0 a θ S ha0 ha1 hθ hS).2.2]
   164	  refine integral_nonneg_of_ae ?_
   165	  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae ae_L0_pos] with l hl
   166	  exact weight_nonneg μ hR a θ l ha0 hθ hl
   167	
   168	/-- `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (main TeX lines 836-841, proof 894-913)
   169	in full, both lower and upper bounds, for a general measure: `μ` s-finite with
   170	`∫(1+|ξ|²)⁻¹ dμ < ∞` and `μ{0} = 0`, `0 < a < 1`, `θ > 0`, the integrand of
   171	`N₁(θ)` for `μ` integrable on `(0,∞)`, `g` measurable with values in `[0,1]`,
   172	`S ⊆ S'` measurable.  Conclusions: the integrand of `N_{1,g,S}` is integrable,
   173	`0 ≤ N_{1,g,S}(θ) ≤ N_{1,1,S'}(θ)`; the outer integrands of `N_{2,g,S}` and
   174	`N_{2,1,S'}` are integrable and `0 ≤ N_{2,g,S}(θ)² ≤ N_{2,1,S'}(θ)²`. -/
   175	theorem damped_multiplier_comparison (μ : Measure (Rd d)) [SFinite μ]
   176	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ) (hμ0 : μ {0} = 0)
   177	    (a θ : ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hθ : 0 < θ)
   178	    (hN : Integrable (fun l : ℝ => l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent μ (θ + l)) L0)
   179	    (g : Rd d → ℝ≥0) (hg : Measurable g) (hg1 : ∀ ξ, g ξ ≤ 1) (S S' : Set ℝ)
   180	    (hS : MeasurableSet S) (hS' : MeasurableSet S') (hSS : S ⊆ S') :
   181	    Integrable (fun l : ℝ => l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent (smoothed μ g) (θ + l)) L0 ∧
   182	      0 ≤ N1on a θ S (smoothed μ g) ∧ N1on a θ S (smoothed μ g) ≤ N1on a θ S' μ ∧
   183	      Integrable (N2onOuter a θ S (smoothed μ g)) P2 ∧ Integrable (N2onOuter a θ S' μ) P2 ∧
   184	      0 ≤ N2onSq a θ S (smoothed μ g) ∧ N2onSq a θ S (smoothed μ g) ≤ N2onSq a θ S' μ := by
   185	  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := N1on_smoothed_mono μ hR a θ ha0 hθ hN g hg hg1 S S' hSS
   186	  obtain ⟨h3, h4, h5⟩ := N2onSq_smoothed_mono μ hR hμ0 a θ ha0 ha1 hθ g hg hg1 S S' hS hS' hSS
   187	  exact ⟨h1, N1on_nonneg a θ S _ ha0, h2, h3, h4,
   188	    N2onSq_nonneg _ (smoothed_hR μ g hg hg1 hR) (smoothed_zero μ g hμ0) a θ S ha0 ha1 hθ hS,
   189	    h5⟩

   191	/-! ### (i) The multiplier class and Gaussian multipliers -/
   192	
   193	/-- The multiplier class of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (TeX lines
   194	826-829): `g : ℝ^d → ℝ≥0` measurable with values in `[0,1]`. -/
   195	def IsMultiplier (g : Rd d → ℝ≥0) : Prop := Measurable g ∧ ∀ ξ, g ξ ≤ 1
   196	
   197	/-- The class is closed under pointwise products (TeX lines 845-846 and
   198	915-916: "products of multipliers in `[0,1]` depending only on `ξ`"). -/
   199	theorem IsMultiplier.mul {g h : Rd d → ℝ≥0} (hg : IsMultiplier g) (hh : IsMultiplier h) :
   200	    IsMultiplier (g * h) :=
   201	  ⟨hg.1.mul hh.1, fun ξ => by
   202	    simpa using mul_le_one' (hg.2 ξ) (hh.2 ξ)⟩
   203	
   204	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route (no manuscript step).  Multiplying the
   205	spectral measure by `g` and then by `h` (both measurable) is multiplying it by
   206	`g h`: `h(gμ) = (gh)μ`. -/
   207	theorem smoothed_smoothed (μ : Measure (Rd d)) {g h : Rd d → ℝ≥0} (hg : Measurable g)
   208	    (hh : Measurable h) : smoothed (smoothed μ g) h = smoothed μ (g * h) := by
   209	  unfold smoothed
   210	  rw [← withDensity_mul μ hg.coe_nnreal_ennreal hh.coe_nnreal_ennreal]

211	  congr 1
   212	
   213	/-- The Gaussian multiplier `ξ ↦ e^{-η|ξ|²}`, as a function with values in
   214	`ℝ≥0`. -/
   215	def gaussMult (η : ℝ) (ξ : Rd d) : ℝ≥0 := ⟨Real.exp (-(η * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)), (Real.exp_pos _).le⟩
   216	
   217	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  The real value of `gaussMult`. -/
   218	theorem coe_gaussMult (η : ℝ) (ξ : Rd d) :
   219	    (gaussMult η ξ : ℝ) = Real.exp (-(η * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) := rfl
   220	
   221	/-- For `η ≥ 0` the Gaussian multiplier `e^{-η|ξ|²}` is in the class: it is
   222	measurable with values in `[0,1]` (TeX lines 845-846, 915-916). -/
   223	theorem isMultiplier_gaussMult (η : ℝ) (hη : 0 ≤ η) : IsMultiplier (gaussMult (d := d) η) := by
   224	  refine ⟨Measurable.subtype_mk (by fun_prop), fun ξ => ?_⟩
   225	  show Real.exp _ ≤ 1
   226	  rw [Real.exp_le_one_iff]
   227	  have := sq_nonneg ‖ξ‖
   228	  nlinarith

   230	/-! ### (ii) Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel preserves the mass -/
   231	
   232	/-- The centered Gaussian law on `ℝ^d` with covariance `v I` (`v ≥ 0`), the
   233	image of Mathlib's standard Gaussian `stdGaussian` under `x ↦ √v x`.  It stands
   234	for the heat kernel `p_η` of the TeX (lines 1674, 4698): `p_η = N(0, cη I)` for
   235	the source's normalization constant `c > 0` is `gaussKernel (c η)`. -/
   236	def gaussKernel (v : ℝ) : Measure (Rd d) :=
   237	  (stdGaussian (Rd d)).map fun x => Real.sqrt v • x
   238	
   239	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  `gaussKernel v` is a probability
   240	measure. -/
   241	instance isProbabilityMeasure_gaussKernel (v : ℝ) :
   242	    IsProbabilityMeasure (gaussKernel (d := d) v) := by
   243	  unfold gaussKernel
   244	  infer_instance
   245	
   246	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  Convolution with a probability measure
   247	preserves total mass: `(ρ * ν)(ℝ^d) = ν(ℝ^d)` for `ν` s-finite. -/
   248	theorem conv_univ (ρ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ρ] (ν : Measure (Rd d))
   249	    [SFinite ν] : (ρ ∗ ν) univ = ν univ := by
   250	  rw [Measure.conv, Measure.map_apply measurable_add MeasurableSet.univ, preimage_univ,
   251	    ← univ_prod_univ, Measure.prod_prod, measure_univ, one_mul]
   252	
   253	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  Under `GreenMass G`, every `G_s` with
   254	`s > 0` is a finite measure. -/
   255	theorem isFiniteMeasure_of_greenMass {G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)} (hG : GreenMass G) (s : ℝ)
   256	    (hs : 0 < s) : IsFiniteMeasure (G s) :=
   257	  ⟨by rw [hG.mass s hs]; exact ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top⟩
   258	
   259	/-- `GreenMass` is preserved by convolution with a probability measure `ρ`:
   260	`(ρ * G_s)(ℝ^d) = G_s(ℝ^d) = s` for `s > 0` (for `ρ` the Gaussian `p_η`: TeX
   261	lines 846-847, 916-917). -/
   262	theorem greenMass_conv (ρ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ρ]
   263	    {G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)} (hG : GreenMass G) : GreenMass (fun s => ρ ∗ G s) := by
   264	  refine ⟨fun s hs => ?_⟩
   265	  have := isFiniteMeasure_of_greenMass hG s hs
   266	  rw [conv_univ, hG.mass s hs]
   267	
   268	/-- The separate mass assertion for `N₀` (TeX lines 846-847, proof 916-917):
   269	smoothing the Green family by a probability measure `ρ` leaves `N₀` unchanged,
   270	`N₀^{ρ*G}(θ) = N₀^{G}(θ) = θ^{-2}` for `θ > 0`, with the integrand of `N₀^{ρ*G}`
   271	integrable on `(0,∞)`; hypothesis `GreenMass G`. -/
   272	theorem N0_conv (ρ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ρ]
   273	    {G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)} (hG : GreenMass G) (θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) :
   274	    IntegrableOn (fun s => Real.exp (-(θ * s)) * ((ρ ∗ G s) univ).toReal) (Ioi 0) ∧
   275	      N0 (fun s => ρ ∗ G s) θ = N0 G θ ∧ N0 (fun s => ρ ∗ G s) θ = θ ^ (-(2 : ℝ)) := by
   276	  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := N0_eq _ (greenMass_conv ρ hG) θ hθ
   277	  exact ⟨h1, h2.trans (N0_eq G hG θ hθ).2.symm, h2⟩
   278	
   279	/-- The Gaussian-smoothed wave Green measures `p * G_s` (`p = gaussKernel v`,
   280	`v ≥ 0` not needed) have mass `s` for `s > 0`, `d ∈ {1,2,3}`, and
   281	`N₀(θ) = θ^{-2}`, the value for the unsmoothed `G_s` (`WaveGreen.N0_waveGreen`). -/
   282	theorem gauss_waveGreen_mass (d : ℕ) (hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) (v θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) :
   283	    GreenMass (fun s => gaussKernel v ∗ waveGreen d s) ∧
   284	      IntegrableOn (fun s => Real.exp (-(θ * s)) *
   285	        ((gaussKernel v ∗ waveGreen d s) univ).toReal) (Ioi 0) ∧
   286	      N0 (fun s => gaussKernel v ∗ waveGreen d s) θ = N0 (waveGreen d) θ ∧
   287	      N0 (fun s => gaussKernel v ∗ waveGreen d s) θ = θ ^ (-(2 : ℝ)) :=
   288	  ⟨greenMass_conv _ (waveGreen_greenMass d hd),
   289	    N0_conv (gaussKernel v) (waveGreen_greenMass d hd) θ hθ⟩

   291	/-! ### (iii) Green smoothing as a Fourier multiplier -/
   292

     2	  225| \begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
     3	  226|   Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
     4	  227|   nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
     5	  228|   $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
     6	  229|   convention
     7	  230|   \[
     8	  231|     \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
     9	  232|     \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
    10	  233|   \]
    11	  234|   The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
    12	  235|   when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
    13	  236|   $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
    14	  237|   \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
    15	  238|     \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
    16	  239|   \end{equation}
    17	  240|   with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
    18	  241|   includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
    19	  242| \end{hypothesis}

    22	  494| \begin{proposition}[Jensen lower bound]\label{P:Jensen}
    23	  495|   Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, $\E u(t,x) \ge 1$ and $\E u^2(t,x) \ge (\E
    24	  496|   u(t,x))^2$. Consequently, for every real $\ell$,
    25	  497|   \[
    26	  498|     \liminf_{t\to\infty}t^{-\kappa}\log\E u(t,x)\ge\ell
    27	  499|     \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
    28	  500|     \liminf_{t\to\infty}t^{-\kappa}\log\E u^2(t,x)\ge2\ell.
    29	  501|   \]
    30	  502|   The specialization $\ell = L_*$ is conditional on the intended first-moment
    31	  503|   lower bound with that constant. It is not an unconditional adoption of the
    32	  504|   printed normalization in Theorem~\ref{T:first}.
    33	  505| \end{proposition}
    34	  506| 
    35	  507| \begin{proof}
    36	  508|   For each fixed $t,x$, Lemma~\ref{L:vertex-crude} below gives
    37	  509|   $\sum_n\|X_n(t,x)\|_2 < \infty$; its proof does not use the present
    38	  510|   proposition. Thus, $\sum_n\E|X_n(t,x)| < \infty$, and the mean of the
    39	  511|   canonical series is the sum of its means. By~\eqref{E:expansion}
    40	  512|   and~\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(2.20)--(2.21)}, $\E u(t,x) =
    41	  513|   \sum_{n\ge0}\E S_{2n}(g_{2n}(\cdot,t,x)) \ge 1$, since every term is a pairing
    42	  514|   integral of a nonnegative integrand and $S_0 = 1$. By the Cauchy--Schwarz
    43	  515|   inequality, $\E u^2(t,x) \ge (\E u(t,x))^2$, so $t^{-\kappa}\log\E u^2(t,x)
    44	  516|   \ge 2\,t^{-\kappa}\log\E u(t,x)$. Taking lower limits proves the implication
    45	  517|   for every valid $\ell$. Substituting $L_*$ requires its stated first-moment
    46	  518|   premise. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:Jensen}.
    47	  519| \end{proof}

   185	  101| \begin{lemma}[Deterministic Fourier bound for the spatial energy]
   186	  102|   \label{L:spatial-fourier-bound}
   187	  103|   Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, allowing $\Gamma=0$, let
   188	  104|   $g\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R)$ satisfy $\|g\|_2=1$ and put
   189	  105|   $b=\|\nabla g\|_2^2$. Then $b>0$ and
   190	  106|   \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-fourier-bound}
   191	  107|     0\le A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)
   192	  108|     \le 2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2},
   193	  109|   \end{equation}
   194	  110|   where $R_\alpha$ is defined in~\eqref{E:intro-spectral-mass}.
   195	  111| \end{lemma}
   196	  112| 
   197	  113| \begin{proof}
   198	  114|   If $b=0$, smoothness makes $\nabla g=0$ everywhere. Thus, $g$ is constant,
   199	  115|   and compact support forces $g=0$, contrary to $\|g\|_2=1$. Put $Q=g^2$ and
   200	  116|   use the unnormalized Fourier transform
   201	  117|   \[
   202	  118|     \mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)=\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x.
   203	  119|   \]
   204	  120|   In the unitary convention of Section~\ref{S:masked-covariance}, this is
   205	  121|   $c_d^{-1}\widehat Q$, with $c_d=(2\pi)^{-d/2}$.
   206	  122|   The autocorrelation
   207	  123|   \[
   208	  124|     c_Q(y)=\int_{\R^d}Q(x)Q(x-y)\ud x
   209	  125|   \]
   210	  126|   is smooth and compactly supported. Apply the distributional spectral
   211	  127|   identity~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to this Schwartz function.
   212	  128|   Its inner Fourier integral is $|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2$, since $Q$ is real.
   213	  129|   Hence
   214	  130|   \[
   215	  131|     A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)=\int c_Q(y)\Gamma(\ud y)
   216	  132|     =\int|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi).
   217	  133|   \]
   218	  134|   Both integrals are finite: $c_Q$ is compactly supported and $\Gamma$ is
   219	  135|   Radon, while $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|^2$ is Schwartz and $\mu$ is tempered.
   220	  136|   No density of either measure is required.
   221	  137| 
   222	  138|   Since $\|Q\|_1=1$, we have $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|\le1$. Integration by parts
   223	  139|   and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give
   224	  140|   \[
   225	  141|     |\xi|\,|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|
   226	  142|     \le\|\nabla Q\|_1
   227	  143|     \le2\|g\|_2\|\nabla g\|_2=2\sqrt b.
   228	  144|   \]
   229	  145|   Splitting into $|\xi|^2\le4b$ and $|\xi|^2>4b$ therefore yields
   230	  146|   \[
   231	  147|     |\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\le\frac{8b}{4b+|\xi|^2}.
   232	  148|   \]
   233	  149|   The deterministic resolvent calculation in the proof of
   234	  150|   Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}, together
   235	  151|   with~\eqref{E:intro-spectral-mass}, gives, for $q>0$,
   236	  152|   \[
   237	  153|     \mathcal{R}_\Gamma(q):=\int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{q^2+|\xi|^2}
   238	  154|     =q^{\alpha-2}R_\alpha<\infty.
   239	  155|   \]
   240	  156|   Consequently,
   241	  157|   \[
   242	  158|     A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)\le8b\mathcal{R}_\Gamma(2\sqrt b)
   243	  159|     =2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2}.
   244	  160|   \]
   245	  161|   Nonnegativity follows from the spectral identity. If $\Gamma=0$, then
   246	  162|   $\mu=0$ and both sides of~\eqref{E:spatial-fourier-bound} vanish. This proves
   247	  163|   Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-fourier-bound}.
   248	  164| \end{proof}

    81	/-- Consumer of the wrapper: under `H:homog`, for `θ > 0` and `v ≥ 0` the
    82	Gaussian-multiplied second norm over the full Laplace domain lies between `0`
    83	and `N₂(θ)²`-with-kernel-`K_{(0,∞)}`, and Gaussian smoothing of the wave Green
    84	measures leaves `N₀(θ) = θ^{-2}`. -/

    86	    {Γ μ : Measure (HomogHypothesis.Rd d)}
    87	    (h : HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) (v θ : ℝ) (hv : 0 ≤ v)
    88	    (hθ : 0 < θ) :
    89	    0 ≤ N2onSq alpha0 θ Set.univ (smoothed μ (gaussMult v)) ∧
    90	      N2onSq alpha0 θ Set.univ (smoothed μ (gaussMult v)) ≤ N2onSq alpha0 θ Set.univ μ ∧
    91	      N0 (fun s => gaussKernel v ∗ WaveGreen.waveGreen d s) θ = θ ^ (-(2 : ℝ)) := by

    93	  obtain ⟨-, -, -, -, -, hlo, hup⟩ := h6 θ hθ _ (h7 v hv) Set.univ Set.univ
    94	    MeasurableSet.univ MeasurableSet.univ le_rfl
    95	  exact ⟨hlo, hup, ((h9 v hv).2.1 θ hθ).2.2⟩

   803	\begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
   804	  \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}
   805	  Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the integrals
   806	  in~\eqref{E:damped-norm-definitions} are finite for every $\theta > 0$, with
   807	  $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
   808	  \[
   809	    N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
   810	    N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
   811	    N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
   812	    \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
   813	  \]
   814	  Let
   815	  \[
   816	    K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   817	    \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   818	  \]
   819	  Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
   820	  $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
   821	  $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
   822	  \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
   823	    N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
   824	    N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
   825	  \end{equation}
   826	  More precisely, let $m:\R^d\to[0,1]$ be measurable and let
   827	  $S\subset S'\subset(0,\infty)$ be measurable. Define $N_{1,m,S}(\theta)$
   828	  by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$ and restricting the $\lambda$ integral in
   829	  $N_1$ to $S$. Define $N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2$ by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$
   830	  and the temporal kernel in $N_2^2$ with
   831	  \[
   832	    K_S(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   833	    \int_S e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   834	  \]
   835	  Then, for every $\theta>0$,
   836	  \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}
   837	    \begin{split}
   838	      0\le N_{1,m,S}(\theta)&\le N_{1,1,S'}(\theta),\\
   839	      0\le N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2&\le N_{2,1,S'}(\theta)^2.
   840	    \end{split}
   841	  \end{equation}
   842	  These are comparisons of spectral expressions, including full and tail
   843	  domains. An arbitrary $m$ need not preserve Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}; the
   844	  scaling identities above are asserted for the original covariance only.
   845	  Spatial Gaussian smoothing and Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel
   846	  give multipliers in this class. The separate mass identity for $N_0$ is
   847	  unchanged by Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel.
   848	\end{lemma}
   849	
   850	\begin{proof}
   851	  Scaling the Fourier representation of $\Gamma$ and using Fourier uniqueness
   852	  gives $\mu(cA) = c^\alpha\mu(A)$. Radon finiteness and $\alpha > 0$ then imply
   853	  $\mu(\{0\}) = 0$. In particular, $\mu(B_r) = r^\alpha V$, where $V = \mu(B_1)
   854	  < \infty$. Therefore, for $a > 0$,
   855	  \[
   856	    \int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{a^2+|\xi|^2}
   857	    =\alpha V a^{\alpha-2}
   858	    \int_0^\infty\frac{u^{\alpha-1}}{1+u^2}\ud u<\infty.
   859	  \]
   860	  The last integral is finite since $0 < \alpha < 2$. Substitution into $N_1$
   861	  reduces its finiteness to
   862	  $\int_0^\infty\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}(\theta+\lambda)^{\alpha-2} \ud\lambda <
   863	  \infty$: the conditions at zero and infinity are $\alpha_0 > 0$ and
   864	  $\alpha+\alpha_0 < 2$.
   865	
   866	  For $N_2$ use $|\widehat{G}_s(\xi)| \le \min(s,|\xi|^{-1})$. On $|\xi| \le 1$,
   867	  absolute integration is bounded by
   868	  \[
   869	    V\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty
   870	    e^{-\theta(s+t)}|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}st\ud s\ud t<\infty.
   871	  \]
   872	  On $|\xi| > 1$, use $\int_{|\xi|>1}|\xi|^{-2}\mu(\ud\xi) = \alpha
   873	  V/(2-\alpha)$ and the same time integral without $st$. Both time integrals are
   874	  finite by splitting into $s \le t$ and $t \le s$, then using $u = \min(s,t)$
   875	  and $v = |s-t|$; the only singular factor is $v^{-\alpha_0}$, with $\alpha_0 <
   876	  1$. This proves absolute integrability of the displayed spectral formula. For
   877	  each $\xi$, its time integral is nonnegative because the temporal kernel is
   878	  positive definite. Indeed, it is a positive Laplace mixture of the kernels
   879	  $e^{-\lambda|s-t|}$. This proves $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$.
   880	
   881	  The mass identity $G_s(\R^d) = s$ proves the formula for $N_0$. In $N_1$
   882	  change $\lambda = \theta u$ and $\xi = \theta\eta$. In $N_2$ change $s =
   883	  u/\theta$, $t = v/\theta$ and $\xi = \theta\eta$, using
   884	  $\widehat{G}_{u/\theta}(\theta\eta) = \theta^{-1}\widehat{G}_u(\eta)$. These
   885	  changes give exactly the stated powers.
   886	
   887	  The first tail in~\eqref{E:damped-tail-norms} is a tail of the finite
   888	  nonnegative $N_1(1)$ integral. For the second, $0 \le K_M(r) \le
   889	  |r|^{-\alpha_0}$ and $K_M(r) \to 0$ for $r \ne 0$. The absolute majorant just
   890	  proved permits dominated convergence in $(s,t,\xi)$, giving $N_2^{(M)}(1)^2
   891	  \to 0$. The tail kernel is positive definite by the same Laplace-mixture
   892	  argument, so its quadratic form is nonnegative.
   893	
   894	  For the multiplier comparisons, define
   895	  \[
   896	    B_\theta(\lambda,\xi)=\int_0^\infty\int_0^\infty
   897	    e^{-\theta(s+t)}e^{-\lambda|s-t|}
   898	    \widehat G_s(\xi)\overline{\widehat G_t(\xi)}\ud s\ud t.
   899	  \]
   900	  For each $\lambda>0$ and $\xi$, the positive definiteness of
   901	  $e^{-\lambda|s-t|}$ gives $B_\theta(\lambda,\xi)\ge0$.
   902	  The absolute-integrability bound above, $0\le m\le1$ and
   903	  $0\le K_S\le|\cdot|^{-\alpha_0}$ justify changing the integration order:
   904	  \[
   905	    N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2
   906	    =\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   907	    \int_S\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}
   908	    \int m(\xi)B_\theta(\lambda,\xi)\mu(\ud\xi)\ud\lambda.
   909	  \]
   910	  Nonnegativity now proves the second comparison
   911	  in~\eqref{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}. It is used after time integration,
   912	  not pointwise on the oscillating product of wave Fourier kernels. The first
   913	  comparison follows directly from the nonnegative integrand defining $N_1$.
   914	  The choices $S=(0,\infty)$ or $S=(M,\infty)$ give the full or tail bounds.
   915	  Gaussian spatial and Green smoothing contribute products of multipliers in
   916	  $[0,1]$ depending only on $\xi$. Gaussian Green smoothing also preserves
   917	  $G_s(\R^d)=s$, proving its separate assertion for $N_0$. This proves
   918	  Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}.
   919	\end{proof}

   101	\begin{lemma}[Deterministic Fourier bound for the spatial energy]
   102	  \label{L:spatial-fourier-bound}
   103	  Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, allowing $\Gamma=0$, let
   104	  $g\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R)$ satisfy $\|g\|_2=1$ and put
   105	  $b=\|\nabla g\|_2^2$. Then $b>0$ and
   106	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-fourier-bound}
   107	    0\le A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)
   108	    \le 2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2},
   109	  \end{equation}
   110	  where $R_\alpha$ is defined in~\eqref{E:intro-spectral-mass}.
   111	\end{lemma}
   112	
   113	\begin{proof}
   114	  If $b=0$, smoothness makes $\nabla g=0$ everywhere. Thus, $g$ is constant,
   115	  and compact support forces $g=0$, contrary to $\|g\|_2=1$. Put $Q=g^2$ and
   116	  use the unnormalized Fourier transform
   117	  \[
   118	    \mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)=\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x.
   119	  \]
   120	  In the unitary convention of Section~\ref{S:masked-covariance}, this is
   121	  $c_d^{-1}\widehat Q$, with $c_d=(2\pi)^{-d/2}$.
   122	  The autocorrelation
   123	  \[
   124	    c_Q(y)=\int_{\R^d}Q(x)Q(x-y)\ud x
   125	  \]
   126	  is smooth and compactly supported. Apply the distributional spectral
   127	  identity~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to this Schwartz function.
   128	  Its inner Fourier integral is $|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2$, since $Q$ is real.
   129	  Hence
   130	  \[
   131	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)=\int c_Q(y)\Gamma(\ud y)
   132	    =\int|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi).
   133	  \]
   134	  Both integrals are finite: $c_Q$ is compactly supported and $\Gamma$ is
   135	  Radon, while $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|^2$ is Schwartz and $\mu$ is tempered.
   136	  No density of either measure is required.
   137	
   138	  Since $\|Q\|_1=1$, we have $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|\le1$. Integration by parts
   139	  and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give
   140	  \[
   141	    |\xi|\,|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|
   142	    \le\|\nabla Q\|_1
   143	    \le2\|g\|_2\|\nabla g\|_2=2\sqrt b.
   144	  \]
   145	  Splitting into $|\xi|^2\le4b$ and $|\xi|^2>4b$ therefore yields
   146	  \[
   147	    |\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\le\frac{8b}{4b+|\xi|^2}.
   148	  \]
   149	  The deterministic resolvent calculation in the proof of
   150	  Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}, together
   151	  with~\eqref{E:intro-spectral-mass}, gives, for $q>0$,
   152	  \[
   153	    \mathcal{R}_\Gamma(q):=\int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{q^2+|\xi|^2}
   154	    =q^{\alpha-2}R_\alpha<\infty.
   155	  \]
   156	  Consequently,
   157	  \[
   158	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)\le8b\mathcal{R}_\Gamma(2\sqrt b)
   159	    =2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2}.
   160	  \]
   161	  Nonnegativity follows from the spectral identity. If $\Gamma=0$, then
   162	  $\mu=0$ and both sides of~\eqref{E:spatial-fourier-bound} vanish. This proves
   163	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-fourier-bound}.
   164	\end{proof}

    30	/-- Euclidean space `ℝ^d`. -/
    31	abbrev Rd (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
    32	
    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/
    34	def IsTempered {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    35	  ∃ k : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + ‖x‖) ^ (-(k : ℝ))) ∂ν < ⊤
    36	
    37	/-- An even measure: invariant under `x ↦ -x`. -/
    38	def IsEven {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    39	  ν.map (fun x => -x) = ν
    40	
    41	/-- Positive-definiteness of `Γ` as a tempered distribution:
    42	`⟨Γ, φ ⋆ φ̃⟩` is a nonnegative real for every Schwartz `φ`, where
    43	`(φ ⋆ φ̃)(x) = ∫ φ(x + y) conj(φ(y)) dy` and `φ̃(x) = conj(φ(-x))`. -/
    44	def IsPosDefDistr {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    45	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    46	    (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).im = 0 ∧
    47	      0 ≤ (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).re
    48	
    49	/-- `μ` is the spectral measure of `Γ` in the manuscript's convention
    50	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)` in the sense of tempered distributions:
    51	`∫ φ dΓ = ∫ (∫ φ(x) e^{i ξ·x} dx) μ(dξ)` for every Schwartz `φ`. -/
    52	def IsSpectralMeasure {d : ℕ} (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    53	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    54	    ∫ x, φ x ∂Γ =
    55	      ∫ ξ, (∫ x, φ x * Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) ∂μ
    56	
    57	/-- Hypothesis `H:homog`. Let `d ∈ {1,2,3}` and `0 < α₀ < 1`. The spatial
    58	covariance is a nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure
    59	`Γ` on `ℝ^d` with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure `μ`,
    60	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)`; for every Borel set `A` and `c > 0`,
    61	`Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)`; `α₀ + α < 2` (`E:threshold`), with `0 < α < d` or
    62	`α = d = 1`. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on `ℝ^d` a locally finite
    63	Borel measure is a Radon measure. -/
    64	structure HomogCovariance (d : ℕ) (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) :
    65	    Prop where
    66	  dim : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3
    67	  alpha0_pos : 0 < alpha0
    68	  alpha0_lt_one : alpha0 < 1
    69	  Γ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ
    70	  Γ_even : IsEven Γ
    71	  Γ_tempered : IsTempered Γ
    72	  Γ_posdef : IsPosDefDistr Γ
    73	  μ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ
    74	  μ_even : IsEven μ
    75	  μ_tempered : IsTempered μ
    76	  spectral : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ
    77	  scaling : ∀ A : Set (Rd d), MeasurableSet A → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c →
    78	    Γ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ ((d : ℝ) - alpha)) * Γ A
    79	  threshold : alpha0 + alpha < 2
    80	  alpha_range : (0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1)
    81	
    82	/-- The numerical part of `H:homog`, in the form used by `DriverParameters`
    83	(with `a = α₀`). -/
    84	theorem homog_params {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    85	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    86	    DriverParameters.Homog d alpha alpha0 :=
    87	  ⟨h.dim, h.alpha0_pos, h.alpha0_lt_one, by linarith [h.threshold], h.alpha_range⟩
    88	
    89	/-- `E:kappa` with the manuscript's hypothesis: under `H:homog`,
    90	`κ = (4 - α - α₀)/(3 - α) ∈ (1, 2)`. -/
    91	theorem kappa_mem_Ioo_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    92	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    93	    KappaRange.kappa alpha alpha0 ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 :=
    94	  KappaRange.kappa_mem_Ioo d alpha alpha0 h.dim h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one
    95	    h.threshold h.alpha_range
    96	
    97	/-- `E:driver-parameters` with the manuscript's hypothesis (the section
    98	retains `H:homog` and sets `a = α₀`): its strict intervals are nonempty. -/
    99	theorem parameters_nonempty_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   100	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
   101	    ∃ γ θ β : ℝ, (0 < γ ∧ γ < min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2)) ∧
   102	      (1 / 2 < θ ∧ θ < β ∧ β < min (1 - alpha0 / 2) ((3 - alpha0 - alpha) / 2)) :=
   103	  DriverParameters.parameters_nonempty d alpha alpha0 (homog_params h)
   104

    70	    hI A hA c⁻¹ (inv_pos.2 hc), Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Real.inv_rpow hc.le,

   471	/-- **The deterministic Fourier bound** (general form of
   472	`E:spatial-fourier-bound`, TeX lines 106-109; see the module doc).  Let `Γ, μ`
   473	be locally
   474	finite measures on `ℝ^d` with `μ` a spectral measure of `Γ` in the
   475	manuscript's convention (`IsSpectralMeasure`), `μ` homogeneous of degree `α`
   476	(`SpectralHomog.SpectralHomogeneous`) and `α < 2`.  For a real unit
   477	`g ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^d)` with `b = ‖∇g‖₂² > 0` and `Q = g²`:
   478	the autocorrelation `c_Q` is `Γ`-integrable, `|Q̂|²` and `(1+|ξ|²)^{-1}` are
   479	`μ`-integrable, `A_sp(g) = ∫ |Q̂|² dμ ≥ 0`, and
   480	`A_sp(g) ≤ 2^{1+α} R_Γ(1) b^{α/2}` with `R_Γ(1) = ∫ μ(dξ)/(1+|ξ|²)`
   481	(`SpectralHomog.resolvent μ 1`). -/
   482	theorem spatial_fourier_bound {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)} [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ]
   483	    [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] (hsp : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ) {alpha : ℝ}
   484	    (hI : SpectralHomog.SpectralHomogeneous μ alpha) (ha2 : alpha < 2)
   485	    {g : Rd d → ℝ} (hg : IsUnitTest g) (hb : 0 < gradEnergy g) :
   486	    Integrable (autocorr (fun x => g x ^ 2)) Γ ∧
   487	      Integrable (fun ξ => ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2) μ ∧
   488	      Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ ∧
   489	      spatialEnergy Γ g = ∫ ξ, ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2 ∂μ ∧
   490	      0 ≤ spatialEnergy Γ g ∧
   491	      spatialEnergy Γ g ≤
   492	        2 ^ (1 + alpha) * SpectralHomog.resolvent μ 1 * gradEnergy g ^ (alpha / 2) := by
   493	  obtain ⟨hs, hc, hu⟩ := hg
   494	  have hQs : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (fun x => g x ^ 2) := hs.pow 2
   495	  have hQc : HasCompactSupport (fun x => g x ^ 2) :=
   496	    hc.comp_left (g := fun r : ℝ => r ^ 2) (by norm_num)
   497	  have i1 := integrable_autocorr hQs.continuous hQc Γ
   498	  have hR := SpectralHomog.integrable_inv_one_add_sq hI ha2
   499	  set b := gradEnergy g with hbdef
   500	  set q := 2 * Real.sqrt b with hqdef
   501	  have hq : 0 < q := by positivity
   502	  have hq2 : q ^ 2 = 4 * b := by rw [hqdef, mul_pow, Real.sq_sqrt hb.le]; norm_num
   503	  have hRq := SpectralHomog.resolvent_integrable hR q hq.ne'
   504	  have hpt : ∀ ξ, ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2 ≤ 8 * b * (1 / (q ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) := by
   505	    intro ξ
   506	    have h := norm_fourierQ_sq_mul_le ⟨hs, hc, hu⟩ hb ξ
   507	    rw [hq2, mul_one_div, le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)]
   508	    exact h
   509	  have hmeas : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun ξ => ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2) μ :=
   510	    ((fourierQ_continuous (integrable_sq_and_grad hs hc).1).norm.pow 2).aestronglyMeasurable
   511	  have i2 : Integrable (fun ξ => ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2) μ :=
   512	    Integrable.mono' (hRq.const_mul (8 * b)) hmeas (Eventually.of_forall fun ξ => by
   513	      rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg (by positivity)]; exact hpt ξ)
   514	  have heq : spatialEnergy Γ g = ∫ ξ, ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2 ∂μ :=
   515	    integral_autocorr_eq_spectral hsp hQs hQc
   516	  refine ⟨i1, i2, hR, heq, ?_, ?_⟩
   517	  · rw [heq]; exact integral_nonneg fun _ => by positivity
   518	  · rw [heq]
   519	    calc ∫ ξ, ‖fourierQ (fun x => g x ^ 2) ξ‖ ^ 2 ∂μ
   520	        ≤ ∫ ξ, 8 * b * (1 / (q ^ 2 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) ∂μ :=
   521	          integral_mono i2 (hRq.const_mul _) hpt
   522	      _ = 8 * b * SpectralHomog.resolvent μ q := by
   523	          rw [integral_const_mul]; rfl
   524	      _ = 8 * b * (q ^ (alpha - 2) * SpectralHomog.resolvent μ 1) := by
   525	          rw [SpectralHomog.resolvent_homog hI q hq]
   526	      _ = 2 ^ (1 + alpha) * SpectralHomog.resolvent μ 1 * b ^ (alpha / 2) := by
   527	          rw [← mul_assoc, scalar_identity alpha b hb]; ring

   539	    0 < gradEnergy g := by
   540	  obtain ⟨hs, hc, hu⟩ := hg

   542	  have hD : Continuous (fderiv ℝ g) := hs.continuous_fderiv (by simp)
   543	  rcases (gradEnergy_nonneg g).eq_or_lt with h0 | h0

   587	  have := hH.Γ_radon

     2	\label{S:spatial-occupation-foundation}
     3	
     4	Retain a nonzero original covariance from Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} with its
     5	amplitude. Set $a = \alpha_0$, $k = 3-\alpha > 1$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $D =
     6	q-2a > 0$. The scalar $D$ is fixed. All profiles are real. The original positive
     7	temporal exponent and threshold imply $\alpha < 2$; this is the strict
     8	inequality used in the scalar powers and concavity. The finite variational value

    10	Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
    11	
    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.
    22	\end{lemma}
    23	
    24	\begin{proof}
    25	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ gives sigma-finiteness on exhausting balls, and
    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.
    33	\end{proof}
    34	
    35	Put $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) = B_\Gamma(g^2,g^2)$ and $b(g) = \|\nabla g\|_2^2$ on
    36	$H^1$; initially $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is used only for smooth compact profiles
